title: Delineating Oxidation Aspects of an Additively Manufactured Nanoprecipitation-Strengthened Al<sub>0.2</sub>Co<sub>1.5</sub>CrFeNi<sub>1.5</sub>Ti<sub>0.3</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Prealloyed gas-atomized powder of composition Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3, produced for laser powder-bed fusion
recollection.intervention: Selective laser melting to produce dense specimens followed by isothermal oxidation exposures at 800–1000 °C in air
recollection.structure: Nanoprecipitation-strengthened matrix with finely dispersed B2 and L12 precipitates within an fcc solid solution
recollection.mechanism: High‐temperature oxidation driven by preferential Al and Ti outward diffusion, leading to formation of a duplex oxide scale (Al2O3 inner layer, spinel-type oxides outer layer) and coarsening of strengthening precipitates underneath
recollection.results: At 900 °C for 100 h, a continuous Al2O3 layer ~2 μm thick formed with parabolic oxidation kinetics (rate constant ~1×10^-12 g^2 cm^-4 s^-1), while precipitate coarsening increased average particle diameter from ~20 nm to ~60 nm

score.note: The recollection misses the central comparison between as-printed and 750°C/50 h aged states and gives unsupported oxidation conditions. It partially identifies an fcc matrix with L12 nanoprecipitates, but mislabels the second precipitate population as B2 rather than L21. The proposed alumina-forming mechanism is wrong: protection arose primarily from a continuous Cr-rich/Cr2O3 layer, with discontinuous inner Al/Ti-rich oxides. The reported oxide thickness, rate constant, exposure time, and precipitate-coarsening values are not supported by the paper.
